recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Future Consent narrative cleanups can consider broader wording quality, but FHIR-11064 itself is already represented and does not require a reconciliation edit.
issue_request: FHIR-11064 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 CBCC change request for FHIR-core Consent section 6.4.1 asking to simplify/replace the Consent resource paragraph about representing interoperable health information privacy consent directives, Consent Statements, and Consent Metadata.
initial_application: Git commit 687d10304fe8c9e42f5ff4e7ff3c322653b167f4 explicitly listed GF#11064 and changed source/consent/consent-introduction.xml from the older exchange-only paragraph to the approved wording that mentions interoperable directives, exchange and enforcement by sending/intermediating/receiving systems, FHIR structures with attached or referenced representations, Consent Statement, and Consent Metadata.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini. Later Published Consent cleanup commit 24a94d510247db95964505364d08c0a287198a9b, for FHIR-27110 and FHIR-27773 through FHIR-27776, moved the FHIR-11064 paragraph from source/consent/consent-introduction.xml into source/consent/consent-notes.xml as part of the Privacy Consent General Model without reversing the FHIR-11064 wording. Community searches found no Zulip or Confluence evidence superseding that Jira/source history.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/consent/consent-notes.xml lines 251-258 already retain the approved FHIR-11064 wording in current build-scope Consent source, and the later reorganization explains why it is no longer in the introduction page.
